label: Helical staircase (bespoke sculptural)
description: Sweeping double-curved sculptural staircase without a central column. Each tread individually engineered. Grand entrance / feature centrepiece.

qa.a: A helical staircase is a continuous curved flight without a central column. The word 'helix' describes a three-dimensional curve — the same shape as DNA, spiral shells and certain plant growth patterns. Each tread is individually engineered because the curve is not carried by a fixed central axis.

Where does the word 'helical' come from?
qa.a: From 'helix' — a three-dimensional curve found in nature (DNA · spiral shells · plant growth). A helical staircase rises while continuously curving, giving it the name.

qa.q: What is a double helix or grand curved staircase?
qa.a: A double helix or grand curved staircase uses multiple sweeping curves — often two staircases that mirror each other. Common in hotels, luxury homes and public buildings as a statement staircase. Requires complex structure and high craftsmanship.
An oval staircase is a curved layout where the plan is a stretched circle. It gives a softer flow than straight stairs and a wider visual field of view, with a premium architectural appearance.
